phylogeography of a pathogen can be used as a diagnostic for the underlying ecology, and this approach can be used to test ecological hypotheses.
the genetic structure of a pathogenic RNA virus can be used as a diagnostic tool for the ecology of the disease.
the phylogenetic structure of RNA viruses, as revealed by molecular evolutionary signatures, is shaped by ecological factors and can be used to infer host ecological dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic structure of an RNA pathogen is an accurate reflection of its host population's ecological structure.
phylogeographic patterns can be used as an ecological indicator of host population movement, and that these patterns can be used to infer the rate of population movement.
phylogeographic analysis can reveal ecological processes and that phylogeography is more revealing of ecological process than demography alone.

the evolutionary signatures of ecological dynamics are not always apparent and may be obscured by stochastic processes.
phylogenetic and epidemiological data can be used in concert to understand ecological process, even in the absence of ecological observations.
